items.followUp: Differentiate between Bus Topology and Mesh Topology, and state two advantages of each.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the basic arrangements of star and ring topologies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the central connecting device in star topology and the closed-loop arrangement in ring topology.

rubric.why: Identifies two valid advantages of star topology.
rubric.description: Gives two advantages of star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct advantages.

accept: each computer connects to two others
rubric.why: Describes how devices are connected in ring topology.
rubric.description: Correctly describes the ring arrangement or data path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of the ring arrangement or data transmission around it.

rubric.why: Identifies two valid advantages of ring topology.
rubric.description: Gives two advantages of ring topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct advantages.

modelAnswer: Star topology: Each computer is connected to a central hub or switch.
Two advantages of star topology are that it is easy to add or remove a computer and a fault in one computer usually does not affect the others.
Ring topology: Each computer is connected to two neighbouring computers, forming a closed loop.
Two advantages of ring topology are orderly data transmission and equal access for the computers on the network.

items.followUp: Name four ethical issues related to data security and explain any three.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of the commonly listed ethical issues concerning information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the issues of privacy, accuracy, property/ownership, and accessibility.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of privacy as control over personal information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that personal information should be protected from unauthorized access or disclosure.

rubric.why: Checks understanding that information should be correct and reliable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that stored data should be correct, reliable, and kept up to date.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of ownership rights over data and software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that data or software belongs to its owner and should not be copied or used without permission.

modelAnswer: The ethical issues related to information are privacy, accuracy, property (ownership), and accessibility.
Privacy means protecting personal information from unauthorized access or disclosure.
Accuracy means that information should be correct, reliable, and kept up to date.
Property means respecting the ownership and copyright of data or software and not using it without permission.

items.followUp: List the main steps used to solve a problem with a computer.

rubric.why: A solution begins by understanding what is required and identifying the relevant data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing problem analysis, including identifying inputs and expected outputs.

rubric.why: Checks that the student knows a solution is designed, implemented, and checked.
rubric.description: Describes the solution, implementation, and checking steps.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the main steps such as designing an algorithm or flowchart, coding, and testing/debugging.

modelAnswer: First, analyze the problem and identify its inputs, processing requirements, and expected outputs.
Then design an algorithm or flowchart, write the program, and test and debug it.

items.followUp: Give two ways in which a flowchart helps while developing a program.

rubric.why: A flowchart makes the sequence and logic of a solution easier to see.
rubric.description: States that flowcharts visually represent a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a flowchart shows the steps or logic of a problem visually.

rubric.why: Flowcharts help people review, communicate, and implement a proposed solution.
rubric.description: States another use in problem solving.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid use such as finding errors before coding, communicating the solution, or guiding program writing.

modelAnswer: A flowchart presents the steps and logic of a solution visually, so the problem is easier to understand.
It helps communicate the solution and identify errors before coding the program.

items.followUp: State one advantage and one disadvantage of using an algorithm to solve a problem.

rubric.why: Checks for a valid advantage of algorithms.
rubric.description: Gives an advantage of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid advantage, such as being easy to follow, language independent, or helping with coding and debugging.

rubric.why: Checks for a valid limitation of algorithms.
rubric.description: Gives a disadvantage of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid disadvantage, such as becoming lengthy or time-consuming for a large or complex problem.

modelAnswer: Advantage: An algorithm gives a clear, step-by-step solution and is independent of any particular programming language.
Disadvantage: An algorithm can become lengthy and time-consuming to write for a large or complex problem.

items.followUp: What is invalid test data? Give one example.

rubric.why: A valid test value must meet the program's input requirements.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that it is test data of the correct type and within the acceptable range or otherwise meets the stated input requirements; award 1 mark for a partially correct definition.

modelAnswer: Valid test data is input data that meets the program's requirements, including the required type and acceptable range.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the anchor tag in HTML?

rubric.why: Checks identification of the HTML anchor element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the anchor tag as <a>.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of what an anchor is used for.
rubric.description: States the purpose of an anchor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it creates a hyperlink to another page or location.

modelAnswer: An anchor is an HTML element written with the <a> tag.
It is used to create a hyperlink to another web page or a location in a page.
